subject: Advice on using count data with uncertainty as census data in IPMs (JAGS)

messages.author: 3e911bc3bc76c82d
messages.subject: Advice on using count data with uncertainty as census data in IPMs (JAGS)
parts:
Hi all!

I am doing some test IPMs to see how I can use different data sources of my study population. An interesting approach would be to use count data with associated uncertainty as census data in my IPM. Generally, count data is implemented as C[t] ~ dnorm(N[t], tau), where C is the count data, N is the estimated population size of the model, and tau is the precision estimate. In most IPMs, C is obtained from censuses or surveys and there is only one single measure per year without any associated uncertainty. In my case, I am thinking of estimating C using a model of population size. I have seen that this approach was used before, so it should be possible (see Tempel, Peery, & Gutiérrez, 2014 studying California spotted owls and incorporating population size estimates from an occupancy model as count data). 

I have two potential approaches to address this, but both raise questions I do not know how to address so far. 

1) Ideally, I would like to create a submodel inside my IPM to estimate population size by year. The big issue here is that my estimate of population counts C must be defined at the left side of either a stochastic or a deterministic relationship. E.g.: C[t] <- sum(x[1:10]). Then, whenever I define the stochastic relationship between my estimate of count data and the population size estimate by my IPM's population dynamics process, I must define count data again at the left of the relationship: C[t] ~ dnorm(N[t], tau). To my knowledge, defining C both times at the left side of a relationship should lead to a fatal error as I am defining a variable twice.

2)  Another choice is to create a model to estimate population counts, and then incorporate the result as data for my IPM. The issue here is that my population count results will be formatted as a matrix (years * iterations). At the time of incorporating these data to the IPM, if I incorporated only the means of my results, I would be ignoring all uncertainty associated. If I extracted the mean and sd of every year's count, I would not know how to incorporate both values in the stochastic relationship between counts and population size C[t] ~ dnorm(N[t], tau).

Has anybody here been through this, or know an optimal solution to this situation?

Thank you in advance, have a nice day!

Jaume

messages.author: 312eda23f89ab6c6
messages.subject: AW: Advice on using count data with uncertainty as census data in IPMs (JAGS)
parts:
Hi Jaume,

The first approach is indeed not possible (or at least I do not know how to resolve the problem that you pointed out). However, the second approach that you sketched out is a possible way. Let's assume that you have estimates of annual abundance (i[t]) and an associated SE (SE(I[t])) from your population data. Then there are 2 ways to proceed.
  1. you assume that the errors in the estimated abundance is the same as the errors in the IPM. Then you would use as the observation model in the IPM: i[t] ~ Normal(N[t], SD(i[t])), where N[t] is the population size in the IPM.
  2. you assume that there is additional error in the IPM, e.g. because of lack of fit in other parts of the IPM (more realistic in my opinion). To accomodate additional error, you first 'estimate' a population index as i[t] ~ Normal(y[t], SD(i[t])), and then relate it with the IPM population size as y[t] ~ Normal(N[t], sigma). Sigma is a parameter for which you give a prior and represents the additional error/uncertainty.
You can find descriptions of option 1 in Robinson et al. (2014, 10.1111/2041-210X.12204), and of option 2 in Fay et al. (2019, doi: 10.1111/ecog.04559) and in our IPM book chapter 6.6.4.

Kind regards

Michael
